correctness.rationale: In companion coordinates the two subsequences of coordinate polynomials have degree 2^m in positions 2m and 2m+1. The even leading form is a nonzero pure u-power; restricting the odd leading form to u=0 leaves a nonzero pure v-power. This prevents cancellation in the degree induction and makes the top forms of the two fixed-point equations disjoint at infinity (for n=1 the first equation is v-u, with the same nonzero restriction). No common projective curve component can avoid infinity. Bézout therefore gives the product 2^n in both parities, entirely affine. Independently, introducing the n cyclic scalar coordinates u_i gives equations u_i^2=u_i+(a/c)u_{i+1}-(1/c)u_{i+2}, c=3b/2; this is the same fixed scheme by recurrence elimination and periodicity, including n=1,2 with indices taken modulo n. The monic equations have pairwise relatively prime leading monomials u_i^2 in a graded order, so the squarefree monomials give a quotient basis of size 2^n. A generic target has exactly two preimages, giving topological degree 2, while the iterate degrees give first dynamical degree sqrt(2). For fixed n projective incidence with the singularity condition has closed image on c!=0, since the entire fixed locus avoids infinity. At a=0,c=4, Chebyshev multipliers at scalar fixed points of T_(2^j) have magnitude 2^j away from the endpoints and 2^(2j) at fixed endpoints. The even companion iterates are products and the odd fixed equations reduce to one scalar iterate, so the witness makes every fixed scheme reduced. This verifies the proper exceptional loci, the simultaneous real full-measure assertion, and Möbius inversion/zeta only for distinct points when simple; at exceptional parameters the universally asserted rational expression is for the multiplicity-weighted series.

evidence: G^2 is regular on projective space: its forms on the line at infinity are -cu² and -c(au²+v²), with no common zero. For degree D=2^m the projective intersection count is 1+D+D², the infinity restriction contributes D+1 with simple normal equation, leaving D² affine intersections.

The same regular-map formula cannot be applied to G^(2m+1) on projective space: unequal coordinate degrees leave a base point at infinity. The dynamical-degree article was identified but its full text was not available through the attempted OA DOI retrieval.
